title: SIEM export — RBAC v2, audit schema & evidence automation guidance
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a practical engineering guide for implementing SIEM export connectors from Redwood Inference with a focus on three intertwined areas: RBAC v2 mappings in audit events, a compact audit log schema optimized for Splunk/Datadog/Microsoft Sentinel, and automation patterns for evidence capture required by security/compliance reviews.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: integration engineers, platform security, SREs building or validating SIEM pipelines for customers.
- Scope: connector behaviour, field mappings, examples, redaction rules, and a customer onboarding checklist. Not a protocol spec for new products.

Design goals:
1) Single source audit schema: audits must include stable RBAC v2 references (role_id, grant_type, scope_id) so downstream SIEM / GRC tools can easily correlate changes.
2) Connector-friendly formatting: small consistent JSON envelopes suitable for HEC (Splunk), Datadog logs intake, and Azure Sentinel custom logs.
3) Evidence automation: when high-risk actions happen (role grants, secret rotations, private deployment exports), attach verifiable artifacts to the audit record (snapshot links, cryptographic hashes).

Minimum audit event schema (flat JSON envelope):
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC
- event_id: uuid
- event_type: string (e.g., rbac.role.grant, rbac.role.revoke, config.export.request, model.deploy)
- actor: {type:user|service, id, email} (serialized as actor_type, actor_id, actor_email)
- target: {type, id, name} (serialized as target_type, target_id, target_name)
- rbac_role_id: string (if applicable)
- rbac_grant_type: string (direct|group|inheritance)
- outcome: success|failure|partial
- reason: short text (optional)
- svc_context: string (e.g., hosted|dedicated|private)
- evidence_refs: list of urls (comma-separated string)
- raw_event: base64(JSON) (optional, for forensics)

Note: agents.md requires no nested JSON in the saved doc file itself — above is textual schema for implementers.

SIEM-specific packaging examples:
- Splunk HEC (recommended fields):
  index="redwood-audit" sourcetype="redwood:audit:v2" 
  payload JSON: same envelope; use event_type and rbac_role_id as top-level indexed fields.
  Example payload (plain text):
  {
    "timestamp": "2024-11-07T14:23:01Z",
    "event_id": "0d8f...",
    "event_type": "rbac.role.grant",
    "actor_type": "user",
    "actor_id": "u_12345",
    "actor_email": "eng+alice@redwood.ai",
    "target_type": "team",
    "target_id": "team_qa",
    "rbac_role_id": "role_admin_v2",
    "rbac_grant_type": "direct",
    "outcome": "success",
    "evidence_refs": "https://s3.company/evidence/evt-0d8f-manifest.json"
  }

- Datadog logs: use attributes and tags for fast searchability. Include tags:env:prod,svc:redwood,evttype:rbac.role.grant,role:role_admin_v2.
  Example JSON: same envelope; add "ddsource": "redwood.audit" and "ddtags": "env:prod,svc:redwood,evttype:rbac.role.grant"

- Azure Sentinel / Log Analytics: ship to a custom log table (RedwoodAudit_CL). Use consistent column names like event_type_s, actor_id_s, rbac_role_id_s, evidence_refs_s.

Field mapping guidance (key mappings to SIEM fields):
- event_type -> sourcetype/eventType (indexed)
- timestamp -> _time / TimeGenerated
- actor_email -> userPrincipalName / user.email
- rbac_role_id -> role.id (index/tag)
- evidence_refs -> urls (store as text but keep first URL in a separate indexed_field)

Redaction and PII handling:
- Primary rule: never ship full user credentials, API keys, or plaintext secrets.
- PII fields: actor_email is allowed (to help triage) only if customer explicitly accepts email in export. Otherwise replace with actor_id only.
- Implement field-level redaction policy per export destination. Config flags: redact_emails (bool), redact_ip (bool), redact_raw_event (bool).

Connector reliability & operational knobs:
- Batch window: configurable 500ms–5s; default 1s; keep batch size < 1MB per request for HEC
- Backoff: exponential with jitter; retry up to 5 times then pivot to durable queue (S3/Blob) and alert
- TLS + mTLS option for private customers (support client cert rotation and CA renewal windows)
- Auth: support HEC token, Datadog API key, and Azure managed identity; expose token rotation hooks in platform console
- Observability: emit connector_heartbeat events, export_lag_ms, export_error_count metrics to Redwood Console and to the SIEM itself (with a different event_type)

Evidence automation pattern (recommended):
- Trigger points: rbac.role.grant, rbac.role.revoke, config.export.request, private_deploy.provision, kms.key_rotate
- On trigger: platform will assemble an evidence manifest containing:
  - manifest_id, related_event_id, timestamp, snapshot_location (S3/Blob), signer (service id), manifest_hash (sha256), short human reason
- The manifest is written to the customer-controlled evidence bucket (or Redwood-hosted with restricted ACLs) and its reference URL is added to evidence_refs in the audit event.
- For high-sensitivity actions, also attach signed attestations (JWS) with signature stored in a key vault.
- Helpful automation tip: include a signed change diff (minimal) rather than whole config to keep artifacts small.

Customer onboarding checklist (quick):
- Which SIEM? (Splunk / Datadog / Sentinel / other)
- Allowed fields: do we permit actor_email, raw_event? (customer opt-in)
- Destination auth method: token / cert / managed-identity
- Throughput expectations and retention SLA
- PII handling and redaction policy confirmation
- Evidence artifact hosting: customer bucket or Redwood-managed? Provide bucket ARN or endpoint
- Escalation contact for export failures

Developer notes / TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Add automated conversion utility that maps the flat envelope to Splunk indexes and Datadog tags (prototype in connectors repo).
- Add unit tests that validate redaction flags with sample events.
- Discussion: whether to include full raw_event by default for Dedicated customers (safety vs. cost).

Appendix — quick sample event variants:
- RBAC revoke (short): {timestamp, event_id, event_type: rbac.role.revoke, actor_id, target_id, rbac_role_id, outcome:success, evidence_refs}
- Export request (private deployment): includes svc_context=private and evidence_refs pointing to a signed snapshot URL.

Contact / owner: Aisha Kapoor (security eng) — reach via Slack #sec-siem or aisha.kapoor@redwood.ai
